rows.answer: Job postings expect candidates with dbt knowledge to have solid hands‑on experience (often 2+ years) and deep technical expertise. They should be familiar with core dbt concepts such as models, tests, sources, seeds, snapshots, macros and exposures, and be able to integrate dbt into CI/CD pipelines and automated data workflows. Candidates are expected to design, build, and own production‑grade data products or pipelines, often on modern cloud warehouses like Snowflake or BigQuery, and to apply strong SQL and data‑modeling skills. Senior roles also look for the ability to coach other engineers and contribute to architecture decisions.

rows.question: What do employers mean by experience building RAG pipelines?
rows.answer:
Employers use “experience building RAG pipelines” to refer to the ability to create end‑to‑end Retrieval‑Augmented Generation workflows. This typically includes:
• Designing and implementing document‑ingestion pipelines that chunk raw files (PDF, DOCX, etc.) and generate embeddings.
• Storing those embeddings in a vector database (e.g., Pinecone, Weaviate, FAISS, ChromaDB, Milvus, AWS OpenSearch) and managing indexing and retrieval performance.
• Optimising the retrieval step (vector search, relevance tuning, chunking strategies) and integrating it with LLM prompts for generation.
• Building the pipeline from scratch rather than just configuring out‑of‑the‑box services, often as part of production‑grade AI applications.
These components are mentioned across several postings: document ingestion, chunking, embedding and vector indexing [2]; vector‑database usage and retrieval optimisation [1][3]; and full production‑grade RAG pipeline development [4][5][6].
